body:
Thank you all for attending today! Here are the notes from this meeting (the next one is at https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9132):

### Agenda  
Attendees: @past, @cwilso, @domenic, @josepharhar, @smaug----

1. Review past action items
    1. Someone from WebKit should comment on [Tests for directionality and shadow DOM](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/29820).
        1. Still outstanding.
1. Carryovers from last time
    1. [Domenic] [Sandboxed iframes without allow-same-origin and with about:blank or about:srcdoc urls should not inherit a fallback base url](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9025)
        1. Chrome will continue to explore the best web-compatible solution and come up with a proposal.
1. New topics
    1. [Domenic] [Modernized version of window.open() API](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7485)
        1. Domenic to look into anchor element interactions. Olli to look more into the issue and comment.
    1. [Hsinyi] [Clarify the sequential focusing behaviour when the current focused element is not in the sequential navigation order](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9081)
        1. Joey will explain why Chrome behaves this way. Domenic will clarify his reading of the spec.
    1. [Anne] [Accessibility Attribute Request](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9084)
        1. Will revisit this when Anne is present.
    1. Domenic notes that there are a lot of popover issues in progress, offered to help if people need any help.

### Action Items

1. Someone from WebKit should comment on [Tests for directionality and shadow DOM](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/29820).
1. @domenic to look into anchor element interactions for [Modernized version of window.open() API](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7485). @smaug---- to look more into the issue and comment.
1. For [Clarify the sequential focusing behaviour when the current focused element is not in the sequential navigation order](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9081) @josepharhar will explain why Chrome behaves this way. @domenic will clarify his reading of the spec.
